title: ‘I felt so inspired’: Guardian readers on trying Homer’s epics after seeing The Odyssey

paragraphs.en: “I’m having a classics summer this year,” says Tommy Maddinson, 26, from London. He’s been inspired by Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey to delve into the subject, which has involved cinema trips, visits to the British Museum, and reading Homer’s epic before the film’s release. “I managed to finish it the day before. Since then I’ve been reading a few other classical texts and commentaries …”
paragraphs.zh: “今年我在过一个‘古典学之夏’，”来自伦敦的 26 岁青年汤米·马丁森说。他受到克里斯托弗·诺兰《奥德赛》的启发，深入钻研了这个主题，包括去电影院、参观大英博物馆，以及在电影上映前读完荷马的史诗。“我赶在上映前一天读完了它。从那以后，我一直在读一些其他的古典文本和评注……”

paragraphs.en: Maddinson is not alone. Thanks to the popularity of Nolan’s film, poetry sales in the UK are on course to reach a record high this year after surpassing £8m during the first 30 weeks of 2026 – an increase of 13.3% on the same period last year, according to the market researchers NielsenIQ.
paragraphs.zh: 马丁森并非孤例。得益于诺兰电影的热度，根据市场研究机构尼尔森 IQ 的数据，英国诗歌销售额在 2026 年最初 30 周内突破 800 万英镑——比去年同期增长 13.3%——今年有望创下历史新高。

paragraphs.en: Robert Zoellner, 70, had never read any of the Greek classics because of a “fear” of poetry translations being pretentious and unreadable. “After seeing The Odyssey, I decided to try again,” he says. “I saw on Kindle that Emily Wilson’s translations were available. I found out that if I ignored the fact that it was written in verse and just read it as if it were a normal text, I was really enjoying it.
paragraphs.zh: 70 岁的罗伯特·策尔纳此前从未读过任何希腊经典，因为他“担心”诗歌译本会矫揉造作、难以卒读。“看完《奥德赛》之后，我决定再试一次，”他说，“我在 Kindle 上看到有艾米莉·威尔逊的译本。我发现，如果我忽略它是用韵文写成的，只把它当作普通文本去读，我真的很享受。”

paragraphs.en: Related: It’s not just Homer: the new generation of poets enjoying epic success
paragraphs.zh: 相关报道：不只是荷马：新一代诗人正享受史诗般的成功

paragraphs.en: “I read The Iliad before The Odyssey since it sounds like the proper progression. Agamemnon and Achilles are at each other’s throats, and that’s fun to read about.”
paragraphs.zh: “我先读了《伊利亚特》，再读《奥德赛》，因为这听起来是合理的顺序。阿伽门农和阿喀琉斯斗得你死我活，读起来很有意思。”

paragraphs.en: Kerry Lecomber, 56, from Suffolk, has seen The Odyssey three times and says it has “really stoked” her love “of all things ancient Greece”.
paragraphs.zh: 来自萨福克郡的 56 岁读者克里·勒科姆伯已经看了三遍《奥德赛》，她说这部电影“真正点燃”了她“对古希腊一切事物的热爱”。

paragraphs.en: “I had a place to study classics at age 18 at Leeds University, but it was 1988, and I was far too busy raving and I didn’t get the grades. I’ve always retained a keen interest in the subject. I’ve just started Emily Wilson’s translation of The Odyssey, which my daughter, who studied ancient history at A-level, bought me recently for my birthday.”
paragraphs.zh: “我 18 岁时曾在利兹大学拿到过古典学专业的入学资格，但那是 1988 年，我太忙于狂欢派对，没有拿到理想的成绩。我一直对这个学科保持着浓厚的兴趣。我刚刚开始读艾米莉·威尔逊翻译的《奥德赛》，这是我女儿最近买给我作生日礼物的，她在 A-level 考试中修读过古代史。”

paragraphs.en: She adds: “I’m now looking into finally doing a degree in classics via the Open University. I’ll have to do it part-time while I work full-time, but I know how much I’ll enjoy it.”
paragraphs.zh: 她补充说：“我现在正在考虑通过开放大学终于去读一个古典学学位。我必须在全职工作的同时兼职学习，但我知道我会多么享受这个过程。”
